newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New Hong Kong airport may get too costly - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: New Hong Kong airport may get too costly - watchdog.

text.p: Families flying out of Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport could face huge cost increases, the international airlines watchdog said on Monday.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA), grouping 254 of the world's leading airlines, said Chek Lap Kok (CLK) risked becoming "an airport for the rich" amid rumours that airport user charges would double.
IATA said a doubling of user charges would cost a family of four flying out of Hong Kong an extra $150.

The airport offshore of Lantau island is due to open in April 1998. Hong Kong's Airport Authority has repeatedly said charges for landing and aircraft parking will not be announced until next year after full consultations with the airlines.
But IATA director general Pierre Jeanniot, who recently visited Hong Kong, said he expressed the airlines' deep concerns to the Airport Authority over the proposed increase in charges.

"IATA looks forward to fruitful consultations with the government of Hong Kong in order to arrive at a mutually acceptable solution to the user charges issue which should be based on a gradual approach," he said in a statement.

Industry sources said the Airport Authority is under pressure to recoup massive construction costs. But it is also under increasing pressure from a growing lobby of airlines which see future profit margins under threat from higher fees.
